title: DecisionTrace
description: Schema for DecisionTrace objects — machine-readable records of architectural and editorial decisions about the knowledge graph, public site, and research infrastructure. Stored in workspace/decisions/traces/ as individual JSON files (one per decision). NOT a canonical graph entity type — purely workspace metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for this decision. Convention: YYYY-MM-DD_short-slug

title.description: Short descriptive title of the decision.

rationale.description: Full explanation of why this decision was made. Should include: the problem it addresses, alternatives considered, and why this approach was chosen.

author.description: Person or agent that made this decision.

affectedEntities.description: GRC-20 entity IDs affected by this decision (optional).

affectedFiles.description: Repository file paths affected by this decision.

relatedPatch.description: Patch filename if this decision corresponds to a patch application (e.g., 'patch_1a_fix_cited_in.json').

relatedGraphVersion.description: Graph version produced or affected by this decision (e.g., 'v96', 'v97').

status.description: Whether this decision has been implemented. 'proposed' = documented but not enacted. 'applied' = implemented. 'reverted' = reversed.

revertedBy.description: ID of the DecisionTrace that reverted this decision (if status is 'reverted').

precedents.description: IDs of prior DecisionTrace objects that informed or led to this decision.

consequences.description: IDs of DecisionTrace objects that were triggered by or follow from this decision.

notes.description: Free-text supplementary notes, open questions, or future considerations.

examples.title: Introduce workspace/ authoring layer and two-layer architecture
examples.rationale: The repository lacked a clear separation between the authoring/workshop layer and the public publication layer. Patch files, audit documents, migration scripts, and public site assets were all co-located at the root level. The runbook (docs/sourcequote-migration-runbook.md) referenced scripts that did not exist. This decision introduces workspace/ as the authoring layer and public/exports/ as the publication output target, following a local-first, file-first architecture.
examples.author: mael-rolland.eth
examples.notes: Phase 1 only. No file moves, no canonical graph rewrites, no public site changes.
